patterns.comment: Doc-comment block: %%% on its own line, optional markup tag (md, typ) immediately after, closed by matching %%% on its own line. Spec §05. The trailing `markup.italic` scope is a styling hint for themes that don't already differentiate `comment.documentation` from plain `comment` — every major theme (Dark+, Light+, Monokai, GitHub, …) maps `markup.italic` to an italic font style, so the doc-comment renders visibly distinct from `#` / `###` regular comments out of the box. Users who want a different treatment can override either scope via `editor.tokenColorCustomizations`.
patterns.name: comment.block.documentation.flatppl markup.italic

patterns.comment: Doc-comment line: % with optional markup tag (md, typ) immediately after, content to end of line (engine tokenizer also terminates on ; for transport safety). See the block-form note above re: the trailing `markup.italic` scope.
patterns.name: comment.line.documentation.flatppl markup.italic

patterns.comment: Plain block comment: ### on its own line (with optional leading horizontal whitespace), closed by matching ### on its own line. Spec §05.
patterns.name: comment.block.number-sign.flatppl

patterns.comment: Plain line comment: # to end of line (or to ; — handled by the engine tokenizer; the TextMate grammar highlights to EOL for simplicity).
patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.flatppl

patterns.comment: Hex integer with optional underscores between digits
patterns.name: constant.numeric.integer.hex.flatppl

patterns.comment: Decimal float with fractional part and optional exponent
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.flatppl

patterns.comment: Decimal integer with exponent (sci notation, e.g. 1e7)
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.flatppl

patterns.comment: Decimal integer with optional underscores between digits
patterns.name: constant.numeric.integer.flatppl

hole.comment: Hole _ used inside fn(...) or as a discard name
hole.name: variable.other.hole.flatppl

special-operation.comment: Special operations with their own syntax rules
special-operation.name: keyword.other.special-operation.flatppl

kernel.comment: Built-in distribution constructors and fundamental measures
kernel.name: entity.name.type.kernel.flatppl

higher-order.comment: Higher-order callables and function annotations. `aggregate` (spec §04 §sec:aggregate) is the multi-axis tensor contraction; axis labels `.name` inside its body are picked up by the dot-access pattern.
higher-order.name: entity.name.function.higher-order.flatppl

builtin-function.comment: Built-in functions and value constructors. Spec §07 catalogue.
builtin-function.name: support.function.builtin.flatppl

selector-keyword.comment: Axis selector keywords all/only (spec §05 reserved words, §07 selectors). Match string is synced from keyword-lists.json by gen-grammars.py.
selector-keyword.name: keyword.other.selector.flatppl

reserved-name.comment: Reserved module references and special bindings
reserved-name.name: variable.language.flatppl

patterns.comment: Dot-prefixed broadcast operators and dot-call (spec §05 Broadcasting syntax): `a .op b`, `.op x`, `f.(…)` — sugar for broadcast(...). Listed first so `.==`/`.<=`/etc. munch as one token rather than dot + plain op. `#number` is matched earlier in the file, so the `.` of a trailing-dot real literal (`1.+x` → `1.` then `+`) is never grabbed here (the Julia rule).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.broadcast.flatppl

patterns.comment: Lambda arrow (spec §05 Lambda syntax): `arg -> expr` (single-arg, bare) or `(arg1, arg2, ...) -> expr` (multi-arg, ≥ 2 names) lowers to functionof. `(arg) -> expr` is not valid syntax.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.lambda.flatppl

patterns.comment: Logical operators (&&/||/!). The `!(?![=,\]])` form excludes positions where `!` is the singleton-axis selector inside `[...]` (followed by `,` or `]`) — those match the selector pattern below — and the `!=` comparison form (which is handled in the comparison pattern above by maximal munch, but we still gate to be safe).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.logical.flatppl

patterns.comment: Axis-selector surface symbols `:` (always a slice marker in FlatPPL) and `!` (when immediately followed by `,` or `]` inside `[...]`). Scoped distinctly from arithmetic / logical operators. The keywords `all`/`only` are NOT matched here -- they resolve via the `#selector-keyword` rule under `keyword.other.selector.flatppl`. The `!(?=[,\]])` lookahead matches the singleton-axis usage; bare `!` (logical NOT) is handled by the logical-operator pattern above.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.selector.flatppl

patterns.comment: Aggregate shorthand (spec §05 Axis names + §04 §sec:aggregate): `C[.i, .k] := expr` lowers to `C = aggregate(sum, [.i, .k], expr)`. Listed BEFORE the bare `=` so the multi-char `:=` token wins over `:` `=` lookalikes.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.aggregate.flatppl

patterns.comment: = for canonical assignment; ~ for tilde-binding lowering to draw(...) (spec §05).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.flatppl

dot-access.comment: Matches .name, .name^, or .name_ (§05 axis variance markers). Group 1: dot; group 2: member name (never ends in _ so .nu_ splits as nu + _); group 3: optional variance marker ^ or _, scoped under variable.other.member so it inherits the axis-name colour (`.sigma^` reads as one unit, not name + operator). KNOWN LIMITATION: a field whose name legitimately ends in _ (e.g. .foo_) will have its trailing _ coloured as a variance marker — accepted minor edge; axis names per spec cannot end in _.
